title: TOBA circuit, carnival years and Brown Skin Models
summary: Jones lists TOBA theaters in the South, nine years as comedian with P.J. Tidwell's Carnival from 1928, then the Brown Skin Models until 1941. They discuss when TOBA existed.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: On the TOBA time, we called it then, we played all Chattanooga, Atlanta, Georgia, Memphis, New Orleans, Jackson, Mississippi, Birmingham, Mobile, Alabama, all around through that part of country. When was that about?

Oh, that was in the, I was in, from 40 on, from 1940, during the 40. But from 1928 until 1940, I was with the Vaudeville show then. I stayed on one show nine years down in Texas. P.J. Tidwell's Carnival. I stayed there. I was a leading comedian down there for nine years. And then when I came off of that, then I came back and joined the Brown Skin Models out of New York.
I closed with them in St. Dusty, Ohio in 41.
Well, it wasn't called TOBA after 40, was it? Or is the TOBA?
No, when was the TOBA period?
Back there from, from, well, I say when I ran into it, it was in 28, but there had been TOBA before then.
Yeah, yeah, yeah, that must have, TOBA must have started by the middle 20s sometime, 24 or 25.
You play any Chicago theaters? Haymarket.
Oh, yeah. Played Haymarket Theater. That's the only theater I play in.
